title: Sim-Free Ethos: Feasibility of Same-Day Phantom-Based Adaptive Palliative Radiotherapy
official: A Prospective, Phase II, Single-Arm Feasibility Study of Same-Day, Simulation-Free, Phantom-Based Online Adaptive Palliative Radiation
summary:
This study evaluates same-day, simulation-free adaptive palliative radiotherapy using an online adaptive radiotherapy platform. The study will assess whether image-guided adaptive radiotherapy can be safely and feasibly delivered within a single day for patients requiring palliative radiation treatment. Participants will receive either a single radiation fraction (8 to 20 Gy) or a hypofractionated regimen (25 to 40 Gy in 3 to 5 fractions), based on clinical requirements. The complete treatment workflow, including consultation, consent, adaptive planning, and treatment delivery, will be completed on the same day. The primary outcome is feasibility, defined as successful generation and delivery of a clinically acceptable adaptive treatment plan on the day of consultation. Secondary outcomes include workflow efficiency, acute toxicity, patient-reported outcomes, patient satisfaction, treatment tolerability, and dosimetric comparison between adaptive plans and standard institutional SBRT benchmarks. Approximately 40 participants will be enrolled and followed for up to 12 months.

The study hypothesizes same-day, simulation-free online adaptive palliative radiotherapy is feasible and safe, allowing timely delivery of clinically acceptable treatment plans without compromising treatment quality or patient experience.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 years or older
* ECOG performance status of 0 to 2 at baseline
* Patients who are candidates for palliative radiotherapy
* Patients must have lesions suitable for treatments within the prescribed dose range
* Patients who are able to provide informed consent
* Patients who are available for follow-up for at least one month after treatment (interested individuals will be asked in person)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Prior radiotherapy precluding safe re-irradiation
* Pregnancy
* Comorbidities that can increase radiation risk (such as scleroderma or ataxia-telangiectasia)
* Inability to tolerate supine positioning for approximately thirty minutes
